entries.title: Job 16:1
segments:
CHAP. XVI. 
 
  Job upbraids his friends with unkindness, ver. 1-5.   Bemoans himself, ver. 6-16.   Appeals from their censure to the righteous judgment of God,   ver. 17-22.

entries.title: Job 16:2
segments: V. 2. Such things-These things are but vulgar and trivial.  And so are all creatures, to a soul under deep conviction of sin, or the arrest of death.

entries.title: Job 16:3
segments: V. 3. End-When wilt thou put an end to these impertinent discourses? He retorts upon him his charge, chap.

entries.title: Job 16:7
segments: V. 7. He-God, as appears by the following words.  Weary-Either of complaining, or, of my life.  Desolate-Hast turned my society into desolation, by destroying my children and servants.

entries.title: Job 16:9
segments: V. 9. Eyes-Looks upon me with a fierce, and sparkling eye, as enraged persons use to do.

entries.title: Job 16:10
segments: V. 10. They-My friends.  Gaped-Opened their mouths wide against me.  In all this Job was a type of Christ.  These very expressions are used in the predictions of his sufferings,
. They gaped upon me with their mouths, and
. They shall smite the judge of Israel upon the check.

entries.title: Job 16:11
segments: V. 11. The wicked-And thus Christ was delivered into wicked hands, by the determinate counsel of God.

entries.title: Job 16:12
segments: V. 12. Shaken-As a mighty man doth with some stripling, when he wrestleth with him.  Mark-That he may shoot all his arrows in me.

entries.title: Job 16:13
segments: V. 13. His archers-Whoever are our enemies, we must look on them as God's archers, and see him directing the arrow.

entries.title: Job 16:15
segments: V. 15. I have-So far am I from stretching out my hand against God, chap.

, that I have humbled myself deeply under his hand. I have not only put on sackcloth, but sewed it on, as being resolved to continue my humiliation, as long as my affliction continues. Defiled my horn-I have willingly parted with all my wealth, and power, and glory (as the horn often signifies in scripture,) and been content to lie in the dust.

entries.title: Job 16:17
segments: V. 17. Not-And all this is not come upon me for any injurious dealing, but for other reasons known to God only.  Pure-I do not cast off God's fear and service, chap.
.  I do still pray and worship God, and my prayer is accompanied with a sincere heart.

entries.title: Job 16:18
segments: V. 18. Earth-The earth is said to cover that blood, which lies undiscovered and unrevenged: but saith Job, if I be guilty of destroying any man, let the earth disclose it; let it be brought to light. Cry-Let the cry of my complaints to men, or prayers to God, find no place in the ears or hearts of God or men, if this be true.

entries.title: Job 16:19
segments: V. 19. Witness-Besides the witness of my conscience, God is witness of my integrity.

entries.title: Job 16:22
segments: V. 22. Go-To the state and place of the dead, whence men cannot return to this life.  The meaning is, my death hastens, and therefore I earnestly desire that the cause depending, between me and my friends, may be determined, that if I be guilty of these things, I may bear the shame of it before all men, and if I be innocent, that I may see my own integrity, and the credit of religion, (which suffers upon this occasion) vindicated. How very certainly, and how very shortly are we likewise to go this journey.
